changes: run_v2m_demo_generation.py: new --max_gpu_mem_gb flag caps the process on a shared GPU (used for this run: 14 GB cap next to five training jobs)
tools/render_motion.py: offline SMPL-H mesh renderer (numpy + PIL + ffmpeg), mesh-only or side by side with the source video; no OpenGL, no browser
docs/inference.md: new sections on visualizing the output and running on shared GPUs
.gitignore: ignore output when it is a symlink to bulk storage (the output/ pattern missed symlinks)
narr_run: Now the real run on the bundled example: a five second, nineteen twenty by ten eighty clip at twenty four frames per second, transcoded to thirty. Loading all models took 20 seconds. Detection and tracking took 7 seconds, camera estimation 18 seconds with VGGT Omega on every 10th frame, body feature extraction 460 seconds, and FlowHMR generation itself about 1 second for 151 frames. The whole script finished in 509 seconds, with a peak of 10.2 gigabytes of GPU memory, well under the 14.0 gigabyte cap, on a card that was already running five other jobs.
narr_demo: On the left is the input video. On the right is the motion FlowHMR generated, rendered as the SMPL H mesh in world space with my offline renderer. Watch the feet and the root trajectory: this is exactly the part the physics reward was trained to fix, and it is what the PHC plus controller would be asked to track.
narr_changes: Everything I changed lives on one branch in the fork. First, a memory cap flag for the demo script, so it can share a GPU with other jobs on a cluster. Second, an offline renderer that turns the output motion into a shaded mesh video, or a side by side with the source, without a browser or OpenGL. Third, a gitignore fix for output directories that are symlinks to bulk storage. And a short note in the docs on running on shared GPUs. The branch is pushed to the fork.
